title: Only Christ mediates redemption; yet Saints’ merits move God to grant favors—Mass ‘through the merits of Saints’
source_text: XLVII. Praeterea quamvis doceant Scholae Romanae Theologi nullum esse Mediatorem Redemptionis praeter Christum, cujus mors & obedientia Deo patri praestita unicum est pretium, quo sumus a morte aeterna redempti; pertendunt tamen Sanctos non solum orationibus, sed etiam meritis suis nobis prodesse. Non quod bonis suis operibus nobis proprie meriti sint gratiam & salutem, aliaque quibus egemus beneficia, ut Christus nobis illa promeruit: sed quia Deus Sanctis illorum operibus, & ea qua excelluerunt pietate atque charitate, saepe movetur atque inducitur, ut nobis beneficia varia impertiat; licet ad id nullo jure, aut speciali aliqua promissione obstrictus. Unde est quod in Missae Liturgia Deum orare solent per merita Sanctorum, quorum se putant habere reliquias. Nempe per id Deo quasi ob oculos ponentes egregia illa quae Sancti pro ejus gloria fecerunt, & passi sunt, ut inde facilius & libentius flectatur, ad ea quae petunt ab ipso largiendum.
pass_a_gloss: Moreover although the Theologians of the Roman School teach that there is no Mediator of Redemption besides Christ, whose death and obedience rendered to God the Father is the unique price by which we have been redeemed from eternal death; yet they contend that the Saints benefit us not only by prayers but also by their merits. Not that by their good works they have properly merited for us grace and salvation and the other benefits we need, as Christ promised those things for us: but because God is often moved and induced by the works of those Saints, and by the piety and charity in which they excelled, to impart various benefits to us; although He is bound to that by no right or special promise. Whence it is that in the Liturgy of the Mass they are accustomed to pray God through the merits of the Saints whose relics they think they have. Namely by that placing before God’s eyes, as it were, those outstanding things which the Saints did and suffered for His glory, that He may more easily and willingly be bent to granting what they ask of Him.
pass_b_english: Christ alone mediates redemption; Saints still ‘benefit’ by merits that move God—without strict right or promise.
Mass liturgy asks ‘through the merits of Saints,’ holding their deeds and sufferings before God’s eyes.

lemmas.gloss: through the merits of the Saints

choices.term: nullo jure, aut speciali aliqua promissione
choices.english: by no right or special promise
choices.why: Limits Saintly merit-help vs Christ’s proper merit.
rejected: Saints owe us grace by right
